title: tcspecial simulator configuration
description:
What tcssim needs in order to stand in for the payloads of a tcspecial configuration: how fast each one sends, and what it does wrong. Nothing here describes a payload -- the configuration does that, and the two are joined by name.

A setting written with nothing after it is a setting not stated, which is what the editor writes into the form it makes: every payload of the configuration and every setting a payload may state, so that a reader can see what there is to answer.

tcssim.description: What tcssim itself is told. Required: tcssim does not start without it, and a harness cannot wait for a simulator without knowing where to ask.

ready.description: The UDP address, as address:port, at which tcssim answers whether it has made its stand-ins. One no other run uses: a simulator left running holds it, and a second one started on the same address is refused.

thermostat.description: The hysteresis node of the configuration tcssim stands in for: it reads the simulated sensors whose data reaches that node and switches the simulated heaters the node's data reaches, with the node's setpoint and band, so the loop closes with no tcspecial running. Never with tcspecial running, whose own thermostat switches the same heaters.

seed.description: What the simulation's random numbers start from, so that a run's noise can be had again. Unstated is a seed of tcssim's choosing, which it reports as it starts.

physics.description: The physics model the simulated payloads are attached to: a YAML file of its own, named relative to this file's directory, such as `zone-physics.yaml`. A vehicle's physics outlives any one configuration of its payloads, so it is written once and named by every simulator file that uses it. Its schema is tcspecial-physics.schema.json.

simulated_payload_groups.description: Settings shared by the payloads that name them, each group named by its first key, `group: <name>`. A group says no type: a payload's type is the type it is written under.

simulate.description: Whether the payloads that name this group are simulated: true for tcssim to stand in for them, false for the real devices. A payload in a group that states it does not state it too.

group.description: The group's name, which a simulated payload names with group: to take its settings from it. An entry is named by this, its first key.

protocol.description: Which transport, for a network payload: udp, tcp or unix.

payload_address.description: Where the stand-in answers from, where it has an address of its own to bind.

packet_interval.description: How often it sends, as a length of time -- 1 s, 500 ms -- or the word `continuous` for as fast as the payload can be driven. Nought is no length of time and is refused, being the one value a file arrives at by accident. For a payload that sends on its own: one the configuration gives a trigger is asked instead, at the interval of the payload group it is in, so it states none here and there is nothing for an interval to mean.

segment_interval.description: How often a segment of a packet goes, as a length of time or the word `continuous`; defaults to the packet interval.

drop_percent.description: How often a packet is thrown away.

jitter.description: How late a packet may be, as a length of time, chosen afresh for each one and waited out inside the interval. A length of time and nothing else: leave it out for no jitter.

silent_after.description: How many packets before it stops talking.

close_after.description: How many before it hangs up, where it has a connection to hang up.

ignore_trigger_percent.description: How often it does not answer when it is asked.

connects.description: The terminal of the physics model this stand-in is joined to, as the element's name and the terminal's joined by a dot: `zone.temperature`, `heater_1.on`. Joined to an output, it reports it, in the encoding the conversion -- `to_kelvin` or `to_value` -- its readings go to expects, so the format, the scale and the offset are taken from that node and not stated here. A decision output is sent as `1` or `0`, at once when it changes and again every packet interval. Joined to an input, it drives it with what the vehicle sends -- a decision, or a value in the input's unit -- and sends nothing, being driven the whole of what it is for; its packet interval is how often it looks for what the vehicle sent.

offset.description: How far the place a reporting stand-in is on sits from what its terminal says, in the terminal's unit: `+0.2 K`. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

noise.description: A sensor's random error on each reading: the standard deviation, in its terminal's unit, of the normally distributed noise its electronics add: `0.03 K`. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

accuracy.description: The most a sensor's calibration is off by, in its terminal's unit, as its datasheet's accuracy: `0.5 K`. A fixed error is drawn once a run, normally distributed with a third of this as its standard deviation and never past it. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

drift.description: How far a sensor's error wanders, slowly: the standard deviation, in its terminal's unit, of an error drawn back towards nought with `drift_time` as its time constant. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

drift_time.description: How slowly a sensor's drift wanders, as a length of time. Required with `drift` and refused without it.

lag.description: A sensor's own time constant, as a length of time: how far behind the body it is on it follows. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

simulated_payloads.description: The payloads tcssim stands in for, grouped by type: each entry is one key, `type` and the type, whose value is the list of that type's simulated payloads, each named by its first key, `payload: <name>`. The type is the kind of payload it stands in for, the type the configuration writes that payload under: one of the interfaces a payload is reached over, a payload that is a program being the program itself and needing no stand-in. Said here as well as in the configuration so that a simulator file paired with the wrong configuration is caught rather than simulating the wrong thing.

simulatedType.description: The key of an entry of simulated_payloads: the word type, a space, and a kind of payload.

simulate.description: Whether this payload is simulated: true for tcssim to stand in for it, false for the real device. Required, from this payload or from its group, and not from both: a payload does not override its group's. Empty is not stated.

payload.description: The payload of the configuration this stands in for, by its name: the two files are joined by it. An entry is named by this, its first key.

group.description: A group whose settings this payload takes for whatever it does not state itself.

protocol.description: Which transport, for a network payload: udp, tcp or unix.
